question.problem: The graph of the function $y=f(x)$ passes through $(-2,2)$ and is concave up on the interval $(-3,-1).$ If ${f}^{′}(-2)=-1,$ estimate the value of $f(-1.8)$ using the tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at $x=-2$ and determine whether the approximation is an underestimate or overestimate.
question.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $a=-2$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(-2)+{f}^{′}(-2)(x-(-2)) \\  & =f(-2)+{f}^{′}(-2)(x+2).\end{aligned}
$$

The function passes through the point $(-2,2),$ so we have $f(-2)=2.$ Also, we're told that ${f}^{′}(-2)=-1,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =2+(-1)(x+2) \\  & =2-(x+2).\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $f(-1.8)$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=-1.8.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-1.8) & ≈L(-1.8) \\  & =2-(-1.8+2) \\  & =2-0.2 \\  & =1.8.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the function is concave up on the interval $(-3,-1),$ the linear approximation $L(x)$ is below the graph close to $x=-2,$ and therefore we have an underestimate.
